questions.q: Why does this lesson say 'the DBA owns data quality' is a myth that causes real damage?
options: The person closest to the database rarely has the business context to judge whether data is fit for use — that judgment belongs with the people who use it
DBAs are never qualified to run any data quality checks
Only data consumers are allowed to define quality rules
Database administrators do not have access to the data itself
questions.explain: Fitness for use (Lesson 1) is a judgment call tied to a specific business purpose — context the DBA/custodian role typically doesn't hold alone.

questions.q: In this lesson's house analogy, who is the 'locksmith' — the technical role that implements and runs the checks a steward designs?
options: The data custodian
The data owner
The data consumer
The data governance lead
questions.explain: The data custodian (often a DBA or data engineer) is the technical role responsible for implementing and running the systems and checks.

questions.q: Which role decides what 'fit for use' means for a specific data domain and is accountable for that decision?
options: The data owner
The data custodian
The data consumer
The data steward
questions.explain: The data owner is the business-side leader accountable for a data domain, deciding what counts as fit for use and signing off on the rules.

questions.q: In the lesson's RACI example — 200 new customer rows failing an email validity check — what is the data steward's role?
options: Responsible — investigates the root cause and updates the rule if needed
Accountable — decides whether the failure blocks downstream use
Consulted — confirms whether it's a pipeline issue
Informed — told the data is flagged before using it
questions.explain: The data steward is Responsible in this RACI breakdown: they investigate root cause (Lesson 23) and adjust the rule if it's wrong.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say data consumers are an 'essential, frequently ignored feedback source' for data quality?
options: They are the ones acting on bad output and are often the first to notice something is wrong, even though they rarely get asked
They are responsible for writing all the data quality SQL rules themselves
They own the data domain and are accountable for every failure
They have direct administrative access to fix the underlying tables
questions.explain: Data consumers use the data to do their jobs and frequently notice problems first-hand, but their feedback is often not systematically collected.
